target.title: Fetch MiniMax Token Plan recharge credit balance
target.body:
## Summary

### Token Plan recharge credit balance (original scope)

- MiniMax Coding Plan / Token Plan **remains APIs do not expose the console recharge-credit balance** (积分余额). CodexBar now fetches it from the web console endpoint `GET /backend/account/token_plan_credit` on `www.minimaxi.com` / `www.minimax.io` when a browser session cookie is available.
- Web-session refreshes always attempt the credit fetch after quota/billing enrichment (even when billing history is disabled).
- API-token refreshes merge recharge credits only when an **explicit** manual or environment cookie is configured (not cached browser cookies), using the **resolved API region** after global→China retry and preserving curl `x-group-id` overrides.
- Credit enrichment is best-effort for auth/transport/parser failures but **propagates cancellation** like the other MiniMax optional enrichments.
- `MINIMAX_HOST` selects the matching `www.*` credit host (`minimaxi.com` → `www.minimaxi.com`, `minimax.io` → `www.minimax.io`); use `MINIMAX_TOKEN_PLAN_CREDIT_URL` for custom proxies.
- Global→CN API retry stays **fetch-scoped** only; env-only CLI probes no longer persist `region: cn` into config.
- Diagnostics export includes `pointsBalance`; menu rendering reuses the existing `MiniMax points balance` cost row.

### MiniMax usage summary dashboard (this push)

- Fetch and parse MiniMax **30-day usage summary** (`usage_summary`) alongside quota/credit enrichment.
- Main menu card: inline **6 KPI grid** (today cost, 30d cost, latest-hour tokens, 7d tokens, cache hit, 30d tokens) plus a **cost trend sparkline** when pay-as-you-go pricing is available.
- **Token usage details** submenu: 7d/30d trend chart, daily spend estimates, model breakdown, and window spend KPIs (hidden when the same summary KPIs already appear on the main card).
- **Subscription Utilization** submenu for MiniMax: Session / Weekly quota history chart (same component as Codex/Claude), recording 5h + weekly lanes automatically.
- Menu bar **reset-time mode** now shows the **nearest** MiniMax quota reset (5h window) instead of the weekly reset when both are present.
- KPI formatting: token counts to **2 decimal places**, reset countdowns to **minutes**, localized pricing disclaimer strings.

## Review follow-up (30cf613a)

- [x] **P2 (Codex)** Remove provider-wide region persistence; keep fallback region fetch-scoped
- [x] **P2** Route credit lookups from `MINIMAX_HOST` / resolved region instead of always using global `www.minimax.io`
- [x] **P1** Live cookie-session proof with redacted `diagnose` / `usage` output (below)
- [x] **P3** Gate live test on non-negative balance; optional `MINIMAX_LIVE_TEST_EXPECTED_BALANCE` for exact asserts
- [x] Fall back to `MINIMAX_COOKIE` / env when manual cookie settings are empty
- [x] **P3 (ClawSweeper)** Remove stale region-persistence release note

## Motivation

Users with recharge credits (e.g. 20,000 points in the MiniMax console) saw quota data via API key but `providerCostPresent: false` in diagnostics and no balance in the menu. The balance lives on a separate cookie-authenticated endpoint discovered from the platform web bundle.

This follow-up also surfaces the console usage-summary data CodexBar already had access to: cost/token trends, cache-hit stats, and quota utilization history—without duplicating KPI blocks between the main card and submenus.

## UI evidence (live Plus account, 2026-07-02)

### Main card inline dashboard + credits

![MiniMax main card inline dashboard](https://github.com/Yuxin-Qiao/CodexBar/raw/feat/minimax-token-plan-credit/docs/screenshots/minimax-usage/menu-card-inline-dashboard.png)

Shows 5h / Weekly quota rows, 6 KPI grid, cost trend, top-model line, pricing disclaimer, and **20,000** recharge credits with expiry.

### Menu card usage notes (Settings preview)

![MiniMax menu card usage notes](https://github.com/Yuxin-Qiao/CodexBar/raw/feat/minimax-token-plan-credit/docs/screenshots/minimax-usage/menu-card-usage-notes.png)

### Subscription Utilization (Session / Weekly history)

![MiniMax subscription utilization](https://github.com/Yuxin-Qiao/CodexBar/raw/feat/minimax-token-plan-credit/docs/screenshots/minimax-usage/subscription-utilization.png)

Codex-style quota utilization chart with Session/Weekly lanes; footer shows reset time + used %.

### Token usage details submenu

![MiniMax token usage details](https://github.com/Yuxin-Qiao/CodexBar/raw/feat/minimax-token-plan-credit/docs/screenshots/minimax-usage/token-usage-details.png)

7d/30d segmented trend, daily spend, per-model token/cost rows, and window spend KPIs.

## Test plan

- [x] `make check`
- [x] `swift test --filter MiniMax`
- [x] `swift test --filter MiniMaxTokenPlanCreditTests`
- [x] `swift test --filter MiniMaxUsageSummary`
- [x] `swift test --filter MenuBarMiniMaxResetTimeDisplayTests`
- [x] `swift test --filter UsageStorePlanUtilizationTests`
- [x] Parser coverage for `remaining_credits`, `balance_breakdown.total_balance`, and `total_credits - used_credits`
- [x] Web + API enrichment paths via `ProviderHTTPTransportStub`
- [x] Host-override credit routing + cookie env fallback
- [x] `./Scripts/compile_and_run.sh` — menu card + both submenus verified locally

## Behavior proof

**API-only account (no explicit cookie):** built PR CLI on this branch

```bash
.build/release/CodexBarCLI diagnose --provider minimax --format json --pretty
```

→ `source: api`, quota present, `pointsBalance` omitted (expected; cookie required).

**API key + explicit session cookie (`MINIMAX_COOKIE`, redacted):** built PR CLI on this branch, 2026-07-02

```json
{
  "source": "api",
  "planName": "Plus",
  "pointsBalance": 20000,
  "providerCost": {
    "period": "MiniMax points balance",
    "used": 20000
  }
}
```

Commands:

```bash
export MINIMAX_COOKIE='<redacted _token; minimax_group_id_v2; _sid>'
.build/release/CodexBarCLI diagnose --provider minimax --format json --pretty
.build/release/CodexBarCLI usage --provider minimax --format json
```

Direct endpoint sanity check (same session cookie, redacted): `GET https://www.minimaxi.com/backend/account/token_plan_credit` → `remaining_credits: 20000`, `base_resp.status_code: 0`.

## Notes for reviewers

- Bearer API key alone still cannot read `token_plan_credit` (console returns `not login`); cookie is required for the balance.
- Optional override: `MINIMAX_TOKEN_PLAN_CREDIT_URL`
- Docs: `docs/minimax.md`
- Screenshots also committed under `docs/screenshots/minimax-usage/` for stable PR references.

The PR changes QA Lab Telegram API reads to use the shared bounded provider JSON reader, adds a regression test, and adds a standalone proof script.

PR surface: Source +4, Tests +27, Other +201. Total +232 across 3 files.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): bound Telegram live transport JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/telegram-live.runtime.ts` used an
unbounded `await response.json()` on the Telegram Bot API success path inside
`callTelegramApi`. A misbehaving or hostile endpoint (or accidental huge payload)
could stream oversized JSON and trigger unbounded allocation during `JSON.parse`
while QA Lab live Telegram scenarios poll `getMe`, `getUpdates`, or `sendMessage`.

Replacing the success read with `readProviderJsonResponse` caps JSON parsing at
16 MiB and emits labeled errors such as
`qa-lab-telegram-live.getMe: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`.

This aligns QA Lab's Telegram live transport with the broader OpenClaw response-limit
campaign that already bounded sibling provider and channel surfaces (Telegram plugin
Bot API reads, Copilot token exchange, Google OAuth, search providers, etc.).

## Changes

* `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/telegram-live.runtime.ts`:
  - imports `readProviderJsonResponse` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`
  - replaces `await response.json()` with
    `readProviderJsonResponse(response, "qa-lab-telegram-live.${method}")` in
    `callTelegramApi`

* `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/telegram-live.runtime.test.ts`:
  - adds regression test `rejects oversized Telegram API success bodies` using a real
    `Response` object and asserting the labeled cap error for `getMe`

* `scripts/proof-qa-lab-telegram-bound.mjs`:
  - path-level proof over `node:http` streaming Telegram envelopes plus vitest
    regression hook

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Oversized Telegram Bot API JSON success bodies fail closed
instead of unbounded `JSON.parse` allocation on the QA Lab live transport path.

**Real environment tested:** Node v22.22.0, macOS 24.3.0, `node:http` streaming
server on `127.0.0.1`, built helper from `dist/plugin-sdk/provider-http.js`.

**Exact steps:**
1. Stream an ~18 MiB Telegram `{ ok: true, result: { blob: ... } }` envelope from a
   local HTTP server (no `Content-Length`).
2. Drive `readProviderJsonResponse` with label `qa-lab-telegram-live.getMe` → assert
   labeled parse cap.
3. Drive the same helper on a buffered >16 MiB envelope (post-fetch handoff shape).
4. Verify a normal `getMe` envelope still parses.
5. Negative control: unbounded `response.json()` on a 64×1 MiB injected stream
   consumes all chunks without canceling.
6. Bounded helper cancels early on the same injected stream.
7. Run qa-lab vitest regression via `callTelegramApi("token", "getMe")`.

**Observed result:**
- Parse boundary (stream): `qa-lab-telegram-live.getMe: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`
- Buffered oversized envelope: 16 778 272 bytes rejected before `JSON.parse`
- Normal `getMe` envelope parses with bot username intact
- Negative control: unbounded `.json()` read all 64 chunks; bounded helper stopped at
  readCount=17 and invoked `cancel()`
- `ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED`

**What was not tested:** live Telegram Bot API calls against `api.telegram.org`.

## Evidence

```
=== QA Lab Telegram live transport bound proof (path-level) ===
--- Case 1: oversized streamed Telegram API body rejected at parse boundary ---
  ok: readProviderJsonResponse rejects oversized streamed Telegram body
  ok: parse-boundary label present (got: qa-lab-telegram-live.getMe: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes)

--- Case 2: oversized buffered Telegram envelope (production handoff) ---
  ok: buffered oversized Telegram body rejected before JSON.parse
  ok: body size 16778272 bytes exceeds 16777216 cap

--- Case 3: normal Telegram getMe envelope still parses ---
  ok: getMe envelope parses
  ok: bot identity intact

--- Case 4: negative control — unbounded response.json() ---
  ok: unbounded .json() consumed all 64 chunks (readCount=64)
  ok: stream NOT cancelled via .cancel()

--- Case 5: bounded helper cancels oversized injected stream ---
  ok: readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized injected stream
  ok: stream read stopped early (readCount=17)
  ok: stream cancel() was invoked

--- Case 6: qa-lab Telegram live runtime regression test ---
  Tests  1 passed | 43 skipped (44)
  ok: vitest qa-lab Telegram bound regression test passed

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

```
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test \
  extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/telegram-live.runtime.test.ts \
  -t "rejects oversized Telegram API success bodies"
# Tests  1 passed | 43 skipped (44)
```

New bound regression test (1 added):
- `rejects oversized Telegram API success bodies` ✓
